scope: Unpublished candidate; see docs/payment-family.md for exact implementation boundaries.

families.title: Feature / Composable
families.meaning: One named, readable capability containing state, checks, operations and observations. A clause is not automatically a new document or a sandbox.

parameters.name: editableStates
parameters.meaning: Host lifecycle values during which the instructions may be changed.

bindings.name: lifecycle
bindings.meaning: Read-only lifecycle guard, not a second status maintained by the instructions feature.

actions.amend: {text: Text}. Equal text is a duplicate; changed text is acceptedNew. Only mapped participant connections expose it.

families.status: Native feature example and generic composition substrate. Custom packages provide their own typed checks and result contracts.
families.extensions: An editor-facing typed action/port descriptor, compiler effect analysis and arbitrary native-step action expansion remain specification work. Do not silently treat a BEX action as isolated untrusted code.

families.title: Participants
families.meaning: Names the independent parties and the channels through which their actions are accepted. A role label is not proof of identity.

parameters.name: required
parameters.meaning: Role/channel names that must exist before this fixture-bound document is usable.

actions.validate: Automatic initialization check; no customer-created identity claims are accepted by this check.

families.status: Reuses Core admitted-channel and Timeline Access building blocks. MyOS party IDs are checked by bootstrap. Full representative governance and read-only bootstrap remain future work.
families.extensions: Production principal/provider binding, provider-confirmed Timeline Access, participant replacement, reader grants and pending-to-active access are integration requirements.

families.title: Activation / Acceptance
families.meaning: Collects acceptance of the intended configuration before a business feature may start.

parameters.name: required
parameters.meaning: Each named role must approve. No automatic principal is inferred.

parameters.name: revision
parameters.meaning: Revision each approval must name; stale approvals fail.

bindings.name: state
bindings.meaning: Stores revision, approvals and active flag.

actions.approve: {revision: Integer}; caller must be one of the required roles. Repeated approval is duplicate.

families.status: Native mutual/multiple acceptance. Business actions explicitly check /activation/active.
families.extensions: The same document can intentionally expose preparation before activation. This clause is not a global interceptor. Initializer-level immediate activation and generalized rejection/negotiation rounds are possible variants, not implicitly implemented options.

families.title: Amendments
families.meaning: Changes agreed terms through exact, approved proposals, not by editing a live file and silently reusing previous consent.

parameters.name: approvers
parameters.meaning: Every listed party must approve the proposal.

parameters.name: paths
parameters.meaning: Exact data fields that may be replaced.

bindings.name: state
bindings.meaning: Current revision, pending proposal and accepted proposal history.

bindings.name: editable
bindings.meaning: Business condition that permits a terms amendment.

actions.propose: {proposalId: Text, expectedRevision: Integer, path: JSON Pointer, replacement: BlueValue}; allowlisted path and exact current revision.
actions.approve: {proposalId: Text}; caller must be an approver. Applies only after every required approval; duplicates do not reapply.

families.status: Native allowlisted data amendments with revision matching and multi-party approval.
families.extensions: Installed Connected Clause configuration remains immutable. Arbitrary clause migration, changes to outstanding PI terms and consent-preserving source replacement are NOT implemented. A new PI revision must obtain required confirmations; a data edit never resets financial history.

families.title: Termination / Cancellation
families.meaning: Stops new work and winds down outstanding obligations without pretending cancellation means funds have been returned.

bindings.name: ready
bindings.meaning: Application-defined predicate that outstanding work permits closure.

actions.request: {}; changes Active to WindingDown. Author chooses participant/event connections.
actions.finish: {}; requires readiness and WindingDown. Repeated terminal result is duplicate.

families.status: Native two-phase lifecycle, with separately configured authority and readiness.
families.extensions: New-order and new-payment guards must explicitly use this lifecycle. Refund, payout reconciliation and provider confirmations may remain available during and after wind-down. Arbitrary cleanup, child cancellation and legal consequences are composed business policies, not automatic deletion.

families.title: State Machine
families.meaning: Models one independent dimension of progress with named, validated transitions. Payment, delivery, acceptance and support should not be squeezed into one overburdened status.

parameters.name: subject
parameters.meaning: Readable event subject, e.g. Delivery or Order.

parameters.name: transitions
parameters.meaning: Explicit directed adjacency list. The initial value is authored at the bound state field.

bindings.name: state
bindings.meaning: One scalar state value for this machine.

actions.transition: {to: Text, reason?: BlueValue}; same state is duplicate, other transitions must be allowed. Connection supplies role guards and input mapping.

families.status: Native generic transitions and duplicate-safe same-state handling.
families.extensions: Entry/exit hooks are ordinary connections to transition events. Derived overall status must use business/financial predicates. Evidence review and Milestone packages are meaningful compositions, not additional foundational state interpreters.

families.title: Product
families.meaning: Describes what is supplied inside its host document. Other features can quote, observe or bind to it; a Product need not be a separately embedded document.

parameters.name: currency
parameters.meaning: Currency written with the quote. Cross-currency accounting is not inferred.

bindings.name: product
bindings.meaning: Object replaced by the quote action; preserve descriptions in a separate content field or use a custom product feature.

actions.quote: {unitPriceMinor: Integer[0..1e9], quantity: Integer[1..1000]}; calculates totalMinor and emits Product Quoted. This inherited v2 action still uses legacy hook semantics.

families.status: Existing native quoting primitive plus authored product data consumed by Payment; this example uses fixed amount instead.
families.extensions: Rich booking availability, bundles, content amendment and stock reservation are product-specific feature packages. The delivered quoting action replaces the bound quote object: it must not inadvertently erase independent product text. New connections should prefer a strict outcome adapter before attaching once-only effects.

families.title: Documents
families.meaning: Creates independently identified documents from exact templates and manages explicit links and observations.

parameters.name: allowedFields
parameters.meaning: Only these top-level child input fields can be supplied at creation.

parameters.name: inheritChannels
parameters.meaning: Explicit host role channels copied into the child. No wildcard authority propagation.

parameters.name: sourcePaths
parameters.meaning: Named already-initialized host/peer identities attached under child /sources. Empty path means this host and may establish a deliberate cycle.

parameters.name: identityChildren
parameters.meaning: Uninitialized nested child document roots receiving a deterministic scoped instanceKey before initialization; e.g. /delivery.

bindings.name: template
bindings.meaning: Complete template included in the same application source.

bindings.name: collection
bindings.meaning: An initialized dictionary of generated children; keys are stable and not reused.

actions.start: {key: Text, fields: Object = {}}. Same existing key plus same creation intent is duplicate; conflicting reuse fails.

families.status: Native embedded collection factory with retained creation intent, explicit inherited channels and actual source identities.
families.extensions: The full family also needs attach-existing and non-embedding creation. Those are catalogue/API requirements, not flags this implementation silently supports. A standalone creation mode needs durable publication/delivery ownership. Removing a reference is not erasing a document or canceling its obligations.

families.title: Payment
families.meaning: One named payment feature backed by exactly one independently governed Payment Instruction.

parameters.name: amountMinor
parameters.meaning: Positive explicit amount; use a fixed amount without inventing a Product.

parameters.name: amountPath
parameters.meaning: Host amount field. Takes precedence over direct amount/quote when supplied.

parameters.name: currency
parameters.meaning: Currency for explicit amount. Product quote currency is used for quote fallback.

parameters.name: payer
parameters.meaning: Generic conditional payment: host payer channel. MyOS Account to Account Payment: account ID or Party resolved against the declared roster.

parameters.name: payee
parameters.meaning: Host channel copied as PI seller.

parameters.name: recipient
parameters.meaning: MyOS account ID or Party. Must match exactly one declared party and admitted channel. Manual Bank Payment uses a recipient channel name instead.

parameters.name: guarantor
parameters.meaning: Mandatory accepting/reporting party; fixture executor is combined with this role.

parameters.name: recipientApprovalRequired
parameters.meaning: Require recipient approval in addition to guarantor acceptance.

parameters.name: autoStart
parameters.meaning: Create the PI automatically; false permits explicit start connection.

parameters.name: autoCapture
parameters.meaning: Automatic full-amount capture when all required evidence and financial conditions hold.

parameters.name: requireAll
parameters.meaning: Each named evidence fact is required. Connections are not silently combined by OR.

parameters.name: sources
parameters.meaning: Named accepted peer identities; observers refer to these names.

parameters.name: includeOrder
parameters.meaning: Explicitly connect the host as source order, forming a cycle when needed.

parameters.name: failWhen
parameters.meaning: Persistent failure/compensation intent triggers.

parameters.name: releaseAfter
parameters.meaning: Business confirmation window. One unit only; maximum 365 days. It is NOT an assertion about a real rail authorization expiry.

bindings.name: instruction
bindings.meaning: Exactly one PI slot; never reset it to mean another payment.

bindings.name: product
bindings.meaning: Optional quote fallback, not a required abstraction for payouts.

actions.start: Host action; creates/embeds one PI. On Payment this is automatic unless autoStart=false.
actions.record: PI policy action {fact: Text, confirmed: Boolean}; reusable required evidence, exposed through configured connections.
actions.request: PI lifecycle action {requestId: Text, action: authorize|capture|refund|void, amountMinor?: Integer}; actual names may be authorize/capture/refund/releaseAuthorization connections.
actions.accept / initiate / confirm: PI guarantor operations. accept consents to instruction, initiate supplies transaction correlation, confirm reports a specific command outcome.
actions.fail / advance / retry: PI policy actions. Failure is retained; advance considers both financial outcomes and accepted evidence; retry requires a definitive failed request and consumes that failure once.

events: Payment/Payment Event Received (with originating clause and instructionPath)
families.status: Native method-specific request and confirmation protocols; customer session gate, strict retry entitlement, manual receipt confirmation, and frozen party snapshots. No live external executor.
families.extensions: General installments use multiple Payment instances. Rail-specific expiry, capture/void semantics, disputes, reversal reporting, robust transport outbox and audited retry entitlements require an executor adapter. The custom PI template is the escape hatch; adding arbitrary hooks does not change a frozen accepted financial policy.

families.title: Balance / Ledger
families.meaning: Tracks attributed obligations independently from the cash that a financial institution confirms. Supports exact corrections rather than repeatedly adding the same commission.

parameters.name: currency
parameters.meaning: Human/commercial denomination; this minimal ledger does not automatically type-check every external currency. Application policy must enforce it.

parameters.name: commissionBps
parameters.meaning: Recipe parameter, not the general ledger. Applied per Order to accepted net payment, half-up in integer minor units.

bindings.name: state
bindings.meaning: targets, accrued, paid, reserved and settlement records.

bindings.name: agreements / rate
bindings.meaning: Accepted procurement graph and the agreed commission basis-point field.

actions.setTarget: {key: Text, amountMinor: nonnegative Integer}; computes a delta from that attribution’s old target.
actions.reserve: {key: Text, amountMinor: positive Integer}; only unreserved unpaid obligation may be reserved. Conflicting ID reuse fails.
actions.settle: {key: Text}; marks the reserved settlement paid once. Application must connect this to accepted payment evidence, not an arbitrary untrusted event.

families.status: Native target ledger, correction, reservation and confirmed settlement. Root application binds payout confirmation to the correct PI.
families.extensions: General double-entry journals, reservation release after final payment failure, disputes, FX, account protection and recoupment workflows remain scoped extensions. A post-payout correction leaves paid untouched and exposes overpayment; this is not an automatic debit of a partner bank account.

families.title: Schedule / Timer
families.meaning: Introduces an agreed time source and deadline reactions without treating the current worker clock as an authoritative business fact.

parameters.name: key
parameters.meaning: Readable schedule identity; not a global scheduler ID.

actions.fire: Native action emitting Schedule Fired at the accepted timestamp. Connections use the existing timer syntax: timestamp OR afterEvent+delayMs.

families.status: Native firing helper and existing timer compilation are included. Operation scenarios and a separate signed-completeness timer test qualify the payment deadline.
families.extensions: General recurring calendars, timezone/DST arithmetic, backfill policies, skip/catch-up limits and stop/rearm migrations require an explicit recurrence policy. Membership example opens named periods by an authorized operation; it is NOT automatically monthly billing. Distinct periods still produce distinct Orders and PIs.
